brief: This GS Morning roundup covers five separate desk notes. On Hungary, GS expects the MNB to hold its base rate at 5.50% while cutting its inflation target to 2.5% from 3% today; FX strategy reads the lower target as HUF-positive since it widens inflation differentials versus the euro area, so FX trading stays bullish HUF, fading EURHUF above 365 and holding short PLNHUF as a hedge against Russia-escalation risk. On US inflation, GS ties the Brent rebound from $85 to $100 a barrel to a broader energy shock: it estimates energy and commodity costs have already added about 35bp to year-over-year core PCE, with another 15bp still to come, together just under half of the overshoot behind its 3.1% end-2026 core PCE forecast; it expects headline PCE near 3.5% through year-end before easing to 2.5% by March 2027 and 2.0% by May. On equities, GS derivatives sales flags weaker breadth (31% of S&P names above their 50-day average) and falling positioning sentiment. On rates, a hawkish Warsh press conference and dot plot mean the desk needs softer inflation data to hold in October, while long-end buybacks keep flattening the curve. On KRW, GS expects USDKRW to range 1350-1400.
